title: Short-term rental rules limited to owner-occupied homes
subtitle: Federal enforcement grant, Barrel Yards condominium signing authority, homelessness report endorsement notice, and a public meeting on Erb Street West development.
overview: Council approved new short-term rental rules {{vote:m6}}. Short-term rentals would be allowed only in owner-occupied homes, with limits of 30 consecutive days for one guest and 275 nights a year. Council also approved a grant application to the federal Short-Term Rental Enforcement Fund, which would help pay for software to find and track rentals. Staff will return with a broader update to rental licensing, including low-rise and mid/high-rise rentals, by March 31, 2027. Staff said the aim is to return some rentals to the long-term housing supply, address neighbourhood nuisance concerns and help ensure accommodation taxes are paid.

Council delegated signing authority for the Barrel Yards condominium plan to the Director of Planning {{vote:m7}}. The Mayor tabled a motion endorsing a provincial municipal association report on homelessness; it comes back for consideration on January 27, 2025 {{vote:m8}}.

Council also held an informal public meeting on a proposed commercial expansion, new road and stormwater pond at Erb Street West and Ira Needles Boulevard. No decision was made, and staff will report back later. Council also held a closed meeting on human resources, land and legal matters, and received a 2024 staff year in review.

decisions.detail: Council approved the amending by-law limiting short-term rentals to owner-occupied homes, with a 30-day maximum stay and a 275-night annual cap.
Council approved the city's grant submission to the federal Short-Term Rental Enforcement Fund.
Staff were directed to research, consult and return with a comprehensive rental licensing update by March 31, 2027.
The Director of Planning was authorized to sign and register documents for Draft Plan of Condominium 30CDM-15404.
A motion to endorse the 'Municipalities Under Pressure' homelessness report was tabled for consideration on January 27, 2025.

debate: Councillors asked how many rentals might be in older rent-controlled buildings; staff said no data exists and the grant-funded software should help identify rental types and locations.

Staff said the main enforcement challenge is verifying that owners live where they claim, and that licensing will give data to map problem properties. Councillors raised fines, noting current penalties are $400 and $800 with court options for repeat violations.

Councillors asked about effects on tourism and accommodation tax. Staff pointed to hotel occupancy below the provincial average, said platforms have not consistently remitted the tax, and said they had not yet consulted the local tourism organization.

On the Erb Street West proposal, a landowner's representative to the south objected that the stormwater pond would not take upstream flows and that the road alignment would place costs and land loss mainly on their lands, and asked for a fair resolution before approvals.

The applicant's planner said there is no residential proposed, the roundabout would replace a traffic signal, and talks with the Region and city on timing continue. A councillor questioned whether Council could mediate between private owners; staff said they would normally bring parties together during review.
